title: Gooey Butter Oat Pie
summary: A crunchy toasted oat cookie crust holding a rich, gooey butter filling with a hint of sweetcorn, baked briefly and served cold.
equipment: 20 × 30 cm baking tin lined with baking paper
stand mixer with paddle (or electric hand mixer)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: plus 15-25 g more if the crumbs do not hold

ingredients.item: freeze-dried sweetcorn, ground to a powder
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Bake the oat cookie
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan). Beat the soft butter with both sugars until fluffy, then beat in the yolk. Mix in the oats, flour, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt until it forms a stiff dough. Press it about 6 mm thick into the lined tin and bake 15 minutes, until golden at the edges. Cool completely; the cookie needs to be cold to crumble well.

steps.title: Press the crusts
steps.text: Crumble the cookie into a bowl and rub in the extra brown sugar and salt. Stir in the melted butter until the crumbs clump when squeezed, adding a little more butter if they stay dry. Divide between the two tins and press firmly over the bases and up the sides.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Grind the freeze-dried sweetcorn to a fine powder. In the mixer on low speed, combine the sugar, brown sugar, milk powder, corn powder and salt. Add the melted butter and mix 2-3 minutes, then the cream and vanilla. Finally add the yolks and mix on low just until glossy and even; whipping in air would make the filling puff and crack.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the tins on a baking tray and divide the filling between them. Bake at 175 °C (155 °C fan) for 15 minutes, then turn the oven down to 160 °C (140 °C fan) and bake about 5 minutes more. The pies are ready when the edges are set and lightly browned but the middle still wobbles like thick custard.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Cool on a rack, then freeze the pies for at least 3 hours. Chilling hard sets the buttery centre into its dense, fudgy texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve cold, dusted with icing sugar, cut in thin wedges.

tips: Freeze-dried sweetcorn is sold in health food shops and online; grind it fine for a smooth filling.
A common mistake is baking until the middle is set; it should still wobble when it comes out.
Slice it straight from the freezer or fridge for neat wedges; it softens quickly at room temperature.
safety: EGG NOTE: the soft centre may not reach 71 °C. Use pasteurised egg yolks, or bake 8-10 minutes longer until the centre reads 71 °C; pregnant women, young children, older people and anyone unwell should skip the soft-centred version.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep wrapped in the fridge for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 1 month.
